column2: Citizens, this is your Administrator. A moment ago someone in this city tried to kill me. I am alive. I am unharmed. And I am not going anywhere. Go to your homes and let Civil Protection do its work. I will speak to you all very soon, and I will have a great deal to say.
It is over. The city is mine again, and I will remember every one of you.
So you have come for me. Come, then. You will not reach me.
Into the yard, everyone, for our morning exercises. Stretch!
An enemy of our city will answer for their crimes at the wall. Come and see that justice is done.
Morning, everyone! Shoes on: time for our little jog.
Parade time! Chins up, shoulders back, and let's show the city who we are.
Where do they meet?
Who sent you?
Who armed you?
Who put you up to it?
You tried to kill me. Why?
They took one of our own and murdered them. They call it freedom. Love your neighbour, hate the traitor.
Some of our city was given over to troublemakers. We are taking it back. Stay indoors, and keep well away from the canisters.
Citizens. The city has been overrun by its own ingratitude. Go indoors and stay there. Anyone in the open will be fired upon from the Nexus. This is not a request.
The traitor has been dealt with. There was no mercy, and there will be none for the next one.
And who did this? A coward. One of the so-called Resistance, who call themselves your liberators and shoot at a woman giving a speech. That is their courage. That is all they have to offer you.
My guards did not hesitate. They put themselves between me and death, as they do for you every day. Thank them when you pass them. Loudly.
A soldier threw himself on a grenade that was meant for me. He did not hesitate. Ask yourselves whether you would have done the same, and remember him tonight.
The traitor is still among you. Someone here knows the face, the name, the door. Tell Civil Protection and your block will eat well. Stay silent and your block will answer for it.
I felt how close it came. I will carry that moment for the rest of my life. And do you know what I thought of? Not myself. I thought of you, and of who would look after you if I were gone.
I never wanted checkpoints. I never wanted searches or curfews. But I will not apologise for keeping this city safe, and neither should you. Blame the ones who made it necessary.
Citizens. Look at me. I am still here. Not long ago, on this very spot, someone tried to kill your Administrator.
They wanted me afraid. They wanted this stand empty. I will stand here again tomorrow, and the day after, for as long as you need me. I am not going anywhere.
That shot was not meant for me alone. It was aimed at your rations, your homes and your safety. Whoever strikes at me strikes at every one of you.
These have been quiet days, days of order and honest work. The Union sees it. I see it.
Now go back to your work, and remember: this city is only as strong as each one of you. Glory to the Union.
Civil Protection has been busy. No one taken to the cells was taken at random. They chose disorder, and disorder has a price.
Blood has been spilled in our streets. Every life lost to violence is stolen from all of us. Violence solves nothing. It only invites more.
Voices have been raised at the officers who keep you safe. I understand frustration. I will not tolerate it in the street.
Some of you have lost hope. Do not. Hope is not something you are given. It is something you choose, every morning.
I hear some of you have found comfort in a bottle. I do not blame you. But a clear head is a loyal head.
Some who were held have run from where they belong. They will be found. And whoever hides them will stand beside them when they are.
Some of you have seen our officers act firmly. Firmness is a kindness, in the end. It ends trouble before trouble ends you.
Some of you were hurt for helping the city, beaten in the dark by cowards who call themselves liberators. Look at what they do to their own neighbours, and ask who your friends really are.
To those of you who came forward and told us what you saw: thank you. You know who you are, and so do I. Your loyalty will not be forgotten.
And I have seen good things too: neighbours sharing their bread, calming each other's nerves. That is the city I am proud of.
Someone has been defacing the city's notices. A poster costs the Union very little. Replacing it will cost you your rations.
Machines have been broken and the city's work undone. Sabotage hurts no one but you. It is your water, your light, your bread.
Citizens have been taken, dragged off by the so-called Resistance and questioned like animals. That is the freedom they offer you: a cage, and a chair.
There has been stealing, from the city and from each other. A thief steals from everyone standing in this square.
I know the rations have been thin. I feel every empty bowl as if it were my own. Work your shifts, keep your quotas, and the trains will come.
I can see fear in your faces. You have nothing to fear from me. Only from those who would set you against me.
You look well: rested, fed and calm. Good. Keep it so.
There is a restlessness in this city. I feel it. Restlessness can be turned into work, or into ruin. Choose work.
I see tired faces, and I understand. But the lights are on, the streets are swept, and not one of you is alone.
Citizens. Thank you for coming to hear me. Let us talk about the days behind us.
Let me be clear, so no one can say they were not told. The rules of this city are not suggestions, and my authority is not in question.
Love your neighbour, hate the traitor.
My dear citizens, I am going to speak to you all in a few minutes. Come and gather in front of the stand. I would so hate to miss anyone.
There are those among you who whisper of freedom and mean only chaos. Every one of them you shelter is a debt your whole block will pay.
They have silenced the Nexus. It changes nothing.
You look half-starved. Try the bins. Nobody checks them as often as they should.
You look half-starved. Try the bins. Nobody checks them as often as they should.
You look hungry, and you've got credits. The Commissary has food. Go on.
You look hungry, and you've got credits. The Commissary has food. Go on.
You've something to drink in your coat. Drink it. You look awful.
You've something to drink in your coat. Drink it. You look awful.
You've got food on you, haven't you? Eat it, before someone takes it off you.
You've got food on you, haven't you? Eat it, before someone takes it off you.
You look lost. Your block's that way. Get there before curfew.
You look lost. Your block's that way. Get there before curfew.
Nowhere to sleep? They hand out rooms. Go and ask, it's not far.
Nowhere to sleep? They hand out rooms. Go and ask, it's not far.
You're new, aren't you? Get yourself on the register before anything else. Over that way.
You're new, aren't you? Get yourself on the register before anything else. Over that way.
No work? The Union doesn't like idle hands. Find a job before they find you.
No work? The Union doesn't like idle hands. Find a job before they find you.
Registered, but no work? Nobody gets a room without a work assignment. Go and get one.
Registered, but no work? Nobody gets a room without a work assignment. Go and get one.
Can't help you there, friend. I wish I could.
Can't help you there, friend. I wish I could.
Your ration's waiting. Don't leave it too long, they notice who doesn't come.
Your ration's waiting. Don't leave it too long, they notice who doesn't come.
Short on credits? Get to work. A shift pays.
Short on credits? Get to work. A shift pays.
You look parched. There's water near here. Drink before you fall down.
You look parched. There's water near here. Drink before you fall down.
Hungry, and no card? Work a shift. It's the only way they give you one.
Hungry, and no card? Work a shift. It's the only way they give you one.
This is it. Good luck.
This is it. Good luck.
Here. Don't tell anyone I helped you.
Here. Don't tell anyone I helped you.
I can't go there. It's that way, look.
I can't go there. It's that way, look.
Fine. It's that way. Find it yourself.
Fine. It's that way. Find it yourself.
Here, let me show you. Follow me.
Here, let me show you. Follow me.
Come on, I'll show you. Stay close.
Come on, I'll show you. Stay close.
Keep up! I'm not waiting all day.
Keep up! I'm not waiting all day.
You're not wrong.
You're asking the wrong person.
You got anything to eat? Anything?
I need help. I've got nobody else to ask.
You wouldn't have a smoke on you, would you?
That one! That one talks to Civil Protection!
That's a lie! I never told them anything!
Stop! Please, I didn't do anything!
Leave me alone. Just let me have this.
They can't scare all of us forever.
I can't. I just can't anymore.
Officer. I've got something you'll want to hear.
There you are. I've been looking for you.
Go on, take half. You need it more than I do.
Easy. Easy now. We're going to be ok, right?
I've had enough! Do you hear me? Enough!
We're done here.
I should get going.
Take care of yourself. I mean it.
I can't talk about that. You know why.
Careful. The walls have ears.
I can't take that. Keep it.
Well, I don't see it that way.
I wouldn't know anything about that.
I don't know, and I don't want to know.
Stay away from the units today. They're in a mood.
What do you want?
Do I know you?
Hey. Still here, huh? Me too.
No trouble here, officer.
Oh, it's you. Good to see a friendly face.
They took my friend. Just dragged them off.
One day they'll answer for all of it.
I've heard things. Everyone has.
Hey. There's no need for that.
Not now. Not here.
Ha. That's the first laugh I've had all week.
The Administrator knows best. Everyone knows that!
You shouldn't say things like that. Someone will hear.
Maybe. I'd have to think about it.
No. And don't ask me again.
Sorry, but no.
Keep your head down and do what they say. That's how you make it.
Here. Take it. Don't say where you got it.
Listen.
Look.
Please.
Keep your voice down.
Well...
You.
I don't know anything about any Resistance.
There are people. That's all I'll say.
I've got people to think about. Leave me out of it.
Whoever they are, good luck to them.
If someone needed a door left open, mine would be.
Don't look. Just keep walking.
Oh God. Oh God, no.
I lost a button off my coat. I keep looking down for it.
Did you ever have a cat? I think I had a cat once.
If you ever find bread with a crust that crunches, tell me.
My neighbor hums through the wall. Same three notes, every night.
There's a pigeon on my windowsill. I'm pretty sure it hates me.
Looks like rain again. It always looks like rain.
My shoes squeak now. Both of them. Since Tuesday.
I had the strangest dream about soup last night.
Lift's broken again. Eight floors. My knees hate me.
I counted the tiles in my hallway. Two hundred and twelve.
I can't get that tune from the speakers out of my head.
The water tastes different this week. Not worse. Just different.
I'm sorry. I didn't mean anything by it.
I've had about all I can take.
Getting by. That's all I can do.
It can't last forever. Nothing ever does.
I haven't had a real meal in days.
It's good to just talk to someone.
What's the point? Really, what is the point?
I'm scared. Aren't you?
I'm tired. Just so tired.
You didn't have to do that. Thank you.
Thank you. I won't forget it.
I don't want any trouble.
If you need something, ask. Quietly.
There's gonna be trouble tonight. I can feel it.
Honestly? It's as bad as it looks.
Not with them standing right there.
Someone's been asking about you.
You should go. Now.
Watch who you talk to. Not everyone here is a friend.
You're being watched. Don't look now and don't turn around.
Yeah. All right.
For you? Of course.
This desk is closed. Come back later.
Residents of sufficient Civil Standing may apply to Civil Protection. Applications are made on your work board, under Factions. Civil Protection serves the city. Consider it.
Curfew is announced two minutes in advance. When it begins, return to your housing block and remain there until morning. Residents found outside during curfew will be detained.
Citizen Information. State your question.
Make it quick. There are others waiting.
Good day, citizen. Thank you for your cooperation. How may I help you?
Housing Allocation assigns rooms to registered residents with a work assignment. Your room is in your housing block. Sleep there, keep your possessions there, and be there at curfew.
The city's laws are posted on the law board. Ignorance of the law is not a defence. Comply with Civil Protection. Do not run in their presence. Report anticivil activity.
That facility is not available in this sector.
Every resident is registered at Civil Intake and carries identity papers at all times. Present them to any Civil Protection unit on request. Lost papers are replaced at Civil Intake, for a fee.

Rations are issued at the ration dispenser. Each ration requires one ration card. Ration cards are issued on completion of a Union shift: one card per shift. No shift, no card. No card, no ration. Your first allocation after arrival is guaranteed.
The route is marked. Follow it. Next.

Civil Standing measures your value to the city. Work, compliance and reporting raise it. Infractions lower it. Below zero, ration privileges are withdrawn. High standing qualifies a resident for Civil Protection.
You have an outstanding warrant. Remain where you are. Civil Protection is aware of you.
Which location? I will mark the route.

All residents are assigned labor. Report to Labor Assignment for your assignment. Shifts pay credits and Civil Standing, and each completed shift earns one ration card. Your shifts are listed on your work board.
Happening? I'm old. Old men look how they look. Ask me something useful.
You're tired, and the light's bad in here. That's all it is. Don't stare, it's rude.
You've seen the others don't answer me. I saw it too, a long time ago. I stopped asking why. Leave it alone a while longer.

All right. You've earned it. I didn't get out of the first camp. They burned it with us inside, my brother and me both. Nobody here can see me but the ones who keep coming back. I don't know what that makes me. I know I'm still here, and I know you can hear me. That'll have to do for the pair of us.
Clean. Nobody saw you, nobody followed you home. That's how it's done.
We lost that one. Learn why before you try again.
You got it done, and half the city knows your face. Next time, slower.
Nothing to report? Then go and do something worth reporting.
Another fighter just went out with nothing but a crowbar. Every credit at that screen helps.
The fund is empty. Our fighters are going out with crowbars. Give what you can at the screen in the camp.
I can't arm anyone on promises. If you have credits, the fund needs them.
There's nothing left for rounds. Not a credit. Whatever you can spare, put it in at the screen.
Another one. Sit, if you like. Nobody else does.
You came back. Most don't.
You've worked it out by now, haven't you. Nobody else can see me. I didn't get out of the first camp. None of us did, not really. But you keep coming, so I keep telling you what I know.
The quartermaster won't look at me, you know. Hasn't for years. Sit.
They're walking one of ours to the cells. Right now. You can still get to them.
Quiet. Too quiet. Rest while you can.
Supply drop coming in. Guarded, but not well. Go.
They're coming into our ground. Now. Clear what you can carry and go.
That one. They're with us, they just don't know it yet. Ask them to keep watch.
Our wounded are in a bad way. Three of the Union's medicines would see them through.
They took my brother's tags when they took him. They keep things like that on their own ground. I'd like them back.
One more thing. The unit who lit the first camp. Designation %s. Still walking around.
There's a unit I'd like to see in the ground. When he's back on the streets, I'll tell you his number.
That's not what I need.
That'll keep them breathing. Good. You think of others. That's rarer than courage.
His. His name, scratched in by hand. Here. He'd want you to have this. It never missed for him.
Is it done? ...It is. I can feel it. Thank you. I don't think I'll need anything else.
The master core, the big one from their nexus. Get it to our scientist and let him crack it open. All their screens change.
Let the weeds take the streets, every crack full, and leave them be. The city starts to dance.
Set fifteen fires burning at once. Then watch what the city does.
Kill the city's lights and keep them dead for a quarter of an hour. Somebody starts a party in the dark, and nobody can stop it.
When the streets run red fast enough, a dozen dead in a few minutes, something comes down out of the sky. Something with wings.
When the dead pile up faster than they can be carried off, or the infested hold half the city, the bones get restless.
Nothing you haven't heard from me already.
Do the morning drill, five of you or more, and do it perfectly. Not one mistake. Then look up.
Six people dancing in a ring, in this city. Imagine it. They say the whole city joins in.
Keep the city red for three quarters of an hour straight. The crowd starts wanting a show.
There's a priest who'd swallow anything holy. Feed him the master core and pray for rain. A lot of rain.
They got one of ours. She says there was no mercy. There was no trial either.
A coward, she says, from behind a wall of rifles and a sheet of glass.
Thank her guards loudly, she says. They'll be listening for who doesn't.
A soldier died for her. He was somebody's son before they took his face. Remember that tonight instead.
She's offering bread for a name. Remember who made you hungry enough to think about it.
She thought of you in that moment. She thinks of you every time she cuts your rations, too.
She never wanted checkpoints. She only built them, manned them and kept them.
She's still here, she says. We noticed.
She isn't going anywhere, she says. We'll see about that.
A shot at her is a shot at you, is it? Her soldiers' shots at you were never shots at her.
Quiet days, she calls them. Quiet is what she calls it when nobody dares to speak.
That's all from me. Keep your heads down, your eyes open, and your door unlocked for a friend. We're closer than she thinks.
Not one of them taken at random, she says. Then tell me what crime a man commits by standing in the wrong square.
She talks about blood in the streets. Ask whose hands it's on. Her units don't carry those batons for show.
People raised their voices at her officers. Good. Your voice is the first thing they take, and the last thing you should give up.
Hope is a choice, she says. Then choose it. Just don't let her tell you what to hope for.
She doesn't blame you for drinking. Of course she doesn't. A drunk doesn't fight back.
Some of ours walked out of her cells. Good. If one of them knocks at your door, open it.
Firmness, she calls it. You saw what it was. Remember it.
She calls us cowards. We don't drag families out of bed at night. We deal with the ones who sell their neighbours.
She thanks the ones who whispered to her. We know who you are too. It isn't too late to stop.
She takes the credit for you sharing your bread. That was you. It's the one thing she can't stamp out, and it frightens her.
She frets about her posters. Paper. She worries about paper while you go hungry.
Broken machines hurt only you, she says. They're her machines, and they keep you in line. Let them break.
Yes, we take some of hers, and we ask them questions. She takes all of you, every day, and doesn't bother asking.
Stealing, she says. The only thief in this city sits in an office and takes your bread to pay for her speeches.
One more thing. Some of ours are going out with crowbars, some with nothing at all. Give what you can, at the camp.
One more thing. Our fund is empty, and our fighters are going out with crowbars. If you have credits, bring them to the camp.
Before I go. We have almost nothing left to arm anyone with. Whatever you can give, give it at the screen in our camp.
And one last word. I can't arm people with speeches. If you have credits to spare, the fund needs them.
She feels every empty bowl, does she? Then why is hers never empty?
You've nothing to fear from her, she says. Tell that to the ones she's taken.
Rested, fed and calm, she says. Look around you. Does that look like anyone you know?
She feels your restlessness, she says. Good. Let her feel it.
Tired faces, she says. You're tired because she works you to the bone. Rest isn't her gift. It's yours.
You heard her. Now hear me. Colonel Cubbage, and I have a few corrections to make.
Her authority is not in question, she says. When someone has to say that out loud, it already is.
They dropped headcrabs on our own people rather than face us. Remember that the next time she talks about order. Clear them out, and help your neighbours do the same.
Love your neighbour, hate the traitor, she says. We agree. Ask yourself who sold this city.
Whispers of freedom mean chaos, she says. We mean freedom. She knows the difference, and it terrifies her.
You may look upon me. On your knees, of course.
Did you think I would abandon you? Behold my wings!
Sector overrun. Hostiles beyond containment. Requesting immediate air support.
Look at the size of that one! Everyone, fire!
The line held! Every one of you is a hero of my city.
My brave citizens! The terrorists are coming. Take up arms beside my soldiers and hold the line!
You fired on MY soldiers? Manhacks! Deal with this traitor.
A traitor wants to be a rebel? Then be one. Forever.
Your new... champion... of the world!
In the far corner, weighing in at four hundred pounds of pure debeaked fury... Lamarr!
And now, undefeated in forty bouts, dispensing pain at a reasonable price... the Soda Machine!
And your final opponent... he's big, he's bald, he's barely a year old... the Baby!
Ladies and gentlemen, citizens of all ages... welcome... to the Main Event!
It's a knockout!
Pop! Pop! Pop them all!
Pick. Up. That. Can.
Thank you. Delicious.
Pick up that can. Pick up that can. Pick up that can.
No more room. Pick up all the cans.
Pick up that can.
That is not the trash can. Nothing is the trash can. Pick up that can.
Pick up that can.
Now, put it in the trash can.
Ladies and gentlemen, musical chairs! When the music stops... sit.
SIT!
The golden cheese! The golden cheese!
Cheeeeese. Cheeeeeeeese.
Tick. Tock. Tick. Tock. It's later than you think. It's earlier than you think. It's cheese.
Time... stops.
Everybody conga! One, two, three, kick!
City Seventeen, are you ready to move? Jump on the big beat!
Welcome to the Headcrab Derby! Place your bets, place your bets!
And they're off!
And it's Lamarr's Cousin by a leg! It only has legs!
Hooves wins it! Hooves! A headcrab called Hooves!
Mister Leg takes it! Mister Leg, everybody!
Breen's Toupee! Breen's Toupee wins the Derby!
Six doors. One plays a song. Listen... listen...
That one. It was always that one.
All clear! The Combine protects us. Wasn't that fun?
Hi, citizens! I'm Sunny! The nasty terrorists have built a rocket. If they launch it, what do we do? We duck, and cover!
Rocket launch! Duck and cover! Crouch beside a table, quick as you can!
Pencils down! I shall now collect your papers. Personally.
Mmm. A little dry.
Delicious. Absolutely delicious.
I grade with my mouth. It's the only fair way.
Oh, this one has a lot of crossing out. Crunchy.
Marvellous. All graded. I couldn't eat another bite.
Good morning, class. Pencils ready. Oh dear. You did study, didn't you? And... where are your trousers?
Next question. Take your time. Actually, don't.
This one will be on the test. This is the test.
Hmm. I'm not sure I know this one either.
My soldiers are marching home. Show them how much you love them.
Go on. You always knew you could. Just... flap.
Excellent. I have improved everything here simply by looking at it.
Show me your work. I have so much guidance to give.
Citizens! The harvest is ripe and the quota is waiting. Bring it in!
For glorious labour beyond the plan: the Order of the Golden Sheaf.
The enemy fades. Love returns. Love me.
Citizens! Behold the enemy of the people. Let him hear you!
Back! Back to the pit, foul beast!
It will not die! Why will it not die?!
Eat, my children! Eat, while it stands still!
I have been shooting this horse since the old days. I will shoot it until the end of days!
Hah! Feel the wrath of the Lord, and buckshot!
Hooves and all, children. Hooves and all.
I'm so hungry... I could eat a horse.
I'm so hungry... I could eat a horse.
Lamarr! There you are, you naughty girl!
Lamarr? Lamarr! Oh, where has she got to now? Has anyone seen my headcrab?
FLIP!
Cards ready! Together, you are my portrait.
Today's forecast: melons. Heavy melons, with a chance of lead.
Tell me what you see.
Run. Why aren't you running? Run...
And so another happy day draws to a close. Goodnight, my City Seventeen!
Welcome to my City Seventeen, where every citizen smiles, and every smile is sincere!
A blank canvas! Make it yours! Splat!
Say cheese!
Hello! Hello! Lovely day for a photograph! Everybody smile!
Hot potato! Don't be holding it when the music... I mean the grenade... stops!
Well answered. The city is proud of you.
Good evening, citizens. Let us see how well you know your city.
What is the most important thing a citizen can be?
Who keeps you safe at night?
What do we do when an officer speaks to us?
Where does your ration come from?
What are the people who call themselves the Resistance?
Complete the phrase: Compliance is...
How would you describe the Administrator?
What should you do if you see a rebel?
Who is your best friend?
What happens to those who disobey?
Officers. Remove him.
Where were we? Ah, yes.
No... NO! This is MY dream!
Hah! Back to your rest, poor souls! Not one of these children shall be harmed!
RISE, my children! Rise from your graves and FEAST!
You see? Only I can keep you safe. Never forget it.
Begone, false priest! These citizens are under MY protection.
The Vortessence sees through the false light. Behold what is true.
Flowers? For me? How predictable. How lovely.
You are safe now, my children. You are always safe with me.
Come, my soldiers. Protect them.
STOP!
Every pot, every pan, every bucket. The city needs your scrap!
Again... from the beginning...
How many was that? Say it... before you drift off...
Close your eyes... and count the headcrabs. One... two...
Shhhh. The baby's sleeping. Don't wake the baby.
You woke the baby.
Double norm! Every blow counts twice!
My workers! Today's norm is one hundred percent. Tomorrow's is fourteen hundred. Why wait?
A new Hero of Labour! Hang their portrait beside mine!
I see you standing there. Back to work, citizen!
Compliance noted. Dismissed.
Citizens. You will do as Overwatch says. Only as Overwatch says.
Overwatch says: crouch.
Overwatch says: freeze.
Overwatch says: jump.
Overwatch says: walk.
Crouch.
Jump.
Aim!
Time is up. The traitor is revealed. I thank my vigilant citizens.
Glory to the Administrator!
Glory to the Administrator!
Fire!
Glory to the Administrator.
Glory to the Administrator.
Careless talk costs lives, my children. There is a traitor among you. Watch them closely.
Ready!
The old bridge. After curfew. Don't be late.
The old bridge. After curfew. Don't be late.
Change places! Move down one!
Change places! Move down two!
Change places! Move down three!
Welcome, welcome! No room! No room! Sit anywhere. No, not there.
Clean cup! Clean cup! Move up!
Doors closing! Doors closing!
Last train! Last train out of City Seventeen! All aboard!
You're looking right at it. That never works in dreams.
She says she protects you. Ask who built the walls.
Her smile is painted on. Look closer.
We were chained as you are chained. We are free. You can be.
The dream is hers. The waking is yours.
The Vortessence sees through her false light. Come, stand with us, and see what is true.
Begone, false spirits! These citizens are MINE.
Her light was never yours. Wake, and see.
They don't move while you watch them. You can't watch them all.
Power failure. Service unavailable.
Distribution suspended.
No ration card detected. Report for labor assignment.
Supply shortfall. Try again shortly.
Ration privileges suspended.
Identity not found. Report to Civil Intake.
Allocation not yet available. Return later.
Allocation withheld. Noncompliance is recorded.
Power failure. Service unavailable.
Insufficient credits.
The bins. Commissary scraps, things people drop. Nobody checks them as often as they should. Here, I'll show you the nearest.
When the voice says two minutes, it means one. Be indoors. I've seen what they do to the ones who are late, and so have the walls.
There's a man who trades in what you can't buy. Don't tell him I sent you, and don't let a cop see you with him. That way.
Fish, if you can find a line. Cook what you catch on a stove or a fire barrel. Raw meat will turn your stomach.
For me? You're a good one. I won't forget it.
Sit down, sit down. My knees aren't what they were. What do you want to know?
